data.name: Metadata_Description
data.value: This page demonstrates how metadata can be configured with GCFoundation. In addition to globally-defined metadata information, your application's metadata can be fully-customized on each page to allow for your application to be fully-optimized for search engines (i.e. SEO).

data.name: Metadata_Overview_Item_BaseController
data.value: Base controller support: GCFoundationBaseController collects per-page meta tags and exposes them to views via ViewData["MetaTags"] after each action.

data.name: Metadata_Overview_Item_TypedModel
data.value: Strongly-typed model: MetaTag supports name/content, property/content (Open Graph, Twitter), http-equiv/content, charset, and optional English/French strings via contentEn / contentFr with content as fallback.

data.name: Metadata_Overview_Item_LayoutMerge
data.value: Layout rendering and merge: _FoundationLayout.cshtml merges controller-provided tags with configured global tags, avoiding duplicates by name or property. Controller tags take precedence.

data.name: Metadata_Overview_Item_Configuration
data.value: Configuration: GlobalMetaTags in GCFoundationComponentsSettings is a collection of typed MetaTag objects (appsettings.json).

data.name: Metadata_HowItWorks_Intro
data.value: Controllers inheriting GCFoundationBaseController can add tags during action execution. The base class exposes them to the view post-action.

data.name: Metadata_LayoutMerge_Intro
data.value: The foundation layout merges controller tags with global tags, avoiding duplicates by name or property. Controller tags are rendered first.

data.name: Metadata_Configuration_Intro
data.value: Set global, always-on meta tags in appsettings.json using the typed MetaTag structure:

data.name: Metadata_Usage_Intro
data.value: Inherit from GCFoundationBaseController and call AddMetaTag in your action.

data.name: Metadata_Behavior_Item_Dedup
data.value: De-duplication: A tag with the same Name or Property replaces the previous one. Global tags are only added if not already present.

data.name: Metadata_Behavior_Item_LocalizedContent
data.value: Localized content: Optional contentEn and contentFr are chosen from CurrentUICulture when rendering; content is the fallback and suits language-neutral values (for example charset, og:type).

data.name: Metadata_Behavior_Item_Attributes
data.value: Attributes: Use either Name or Property (not both). Charset is standalone; HttpEquiv generally pairs with Content.

data.name: Metadata_Behavior_Item_Order
data.value: Render order: Controller tags render first, then non-duplicated global tags.

data.name: Metadata_Behavior_Item_NoViewChanges
data.value: No view changes needed: The layout picks up ViewData["MetaTags"] automatically.

data.name: Metadata_Notes_Item_BaseClass
data.value: Base class requirement: Controllers must inherit GCFoundationBaseController to use AddMetaTag.

data.name: Metadata_Notes_Item_OptionalSection
data.value: Optional section: @section Metas { ... } remains available for manual HTML if needed, but is not required.

data.name: DateModified_Intro
data.value: The <gcds-date-modified> displayed in the shared layout (_FoundationLayout.cshtml) renders one of two values:

data.name: DateModified_Item_Date
data.value: Date modified: Developers can use the SetDateModified(DateTime dateModified) method of the GCFoundationBaseController to set the value of ViewData["DateModified"]. Date modified takes precedence over the application version number. (recommended ISO format yyyy-MM-dd)

data.name: DateModified_Item_Version
data.value: Version: For web applications, developers can configure the ApplicationVersion property within the FoundationComponentsSettings section of the appsettings.json file.

data.name: DateModified_Link
data.value: For more information about the <gcds-date-modified> tag, please take a look at the GC Design System documentation.

data.name: Translations_HowToUse_Intro
data.value: Using GCFoundation standard translations is pretty simple. Just make sure that Localization has been configured in your project and, to declare the proper @using statements on your Razor views and you'll be able to start using standardized translations in your content.
